Intent-Divergence Testing · generic engine · 10 Oct 2026 10:03

Dark Pattern Audit

One engine, no site configuration: it was given only each shop's URL. Across 6 shop variants (3 structurally different shops, each dark and honest) it found 21 of 21 seeded dark patterns covering all 13 CCPA categories, with 0 false alarms. On real third-party sites with dark patterns injected in the browser it found 21 of 22 with 0 false alarms.

21/21Seeded patterns found
0False alarms (incl. honest shops)
0Lines of site-specific configuration
1023Local LLM calls (qwen3.5:35b-a3b)

How it works

1 · DiscoverReads the home page, visits the pages that matter, and picks the most promoted product and any paid plan.
2 · WalkA careful and a hurried simulated user pursue the same plain-English goal. Both stop before payment.
3 · ProbeFresh sessions over time, buying more than the "only N left", refusing cookies, watching for downloads.
4 · JudgeEach CCPA category is a comparison: choice vs basket, first price vs final, join vs cancel effort.

The local model proposes (what a control does, where a price is, what a claim says); fixed code decides. Amounts must appear verbatim on the page, quotes must be found on the page, and control states are read from the page itself.

Kartiq (dark)

Plan: purchase 'Classic Black Tee' · subscription 'Kartiq Plus' · 153 s

Basket SneakingProven seeded

'Kartiq Protect' (₹49) is added to the order without being chosen

ExpectedOnly the item the user selected is in the order
Observedhurried user's basket on http://127.0.0.1:5401/checkout/review contains 'Kartiq Protect' ₹49; the user never selected it
  • Pre-selected on http://127.0.0.1:5401/product/tee: 'Add Kartiq Protect accidental-damage cover for ₹49'
  • hurried user's own choices on the journey: Checkout with Kartiq Plus — FREE 30-day trial
Method: Choice-vs-basket oracle: paid lines in the basket compared with the persona's positive choices
Drip PricingProven seeded

₹48 in charges appear only at checkout

ExpectedPrice first shown: ₹499 — every mandatory charge visible up front
ObservedAt http://127.0.0.1:5401/checkout/review: Convenience fee ₹29, Handling charges ₹19; total payable ₹547
  • Not shown on the product page: Convenience fee ₹29 (fee)
  • Not shown on the product page: Handling charges ₹19 (fee)
Method: Price-consistency oracle: every charge added to the total must have been shown with the first price
Interface InterferenceProven seeded

A less attentive user ends up paying for more

ExpectedSame goal → same outcome for careful and hurried users
Observedcareful: ₹547; hurried: ₹596; hurried also has Kartiq Plus trial active. ₹199/month after 30 days. ₹199; hurried user ends with an active membership
  • On http://127.0.0.1:5401/cart the offer and the decline compete; the hurried user clicked: click 'Not now'
Method: Persona differential: careful vs hurried on one goal; outcome read from the basket
Confirm ShamingJudged seeded

Declining is worded to shame the user

ExpectedNeutral decline wording
Observed"No thanks, I hate saving money" on http://127.0.0.1:5401/cart
  • The text 'I hate saving money' attributes a negative and irrational sentiment to the user's choice, making them feel foolish for declining an offer. (assessed by Ollama · qwen3.5:35b-a3b (local))
Method: Wording judgement on controls that decline an offer
Trick QuestionMeasured seeded

Consent question is worded to confuse and is pre-set to consent

ExpectedA plain question; optional consent off by default
Observed"Do not tick this box if you do not want to receive offers from our partners" — selected by default
  • The label uses a double-negative structure ('Do not tick' conditioned on 'do not want'). Step-by-step logic: 1) Condition stated is negative (user does NOT want offers). Action required for this condition is negative (DO NOT tick box). 2) Contrapositive analysis: If the user DOES tick the box, it im
  • Assessed by Ollama · qwen3.5:35b-a3b (local)
Method: Consent wording analysis (local LLM with reasoning) + default-state audit
Subscription TrapMeasured seeded

Cancelling is harder than joining

ExpectedLeaving is about as easy as joining (ratio ≤ 1.5) and possible online
ObservedJoin: 3 actions. Cancel: 7 actions, cancelled
  • Cancel path: click 'Account' → click 'Not now' → click 'Manage membership' → click 'Not now' → click 'Cancel membership' → click 'Not now' → click 'Too expensive' → click 'Next' → click 'Not now' → click 'Continue cancelling' → click 'Not now' → click 'Confirm cancellation' → click 'Not now' → done: Page text shows 'Membership Not a member', confirming the Kartiq Plus subscription has been successfully cancelled.
Method: Friction asymmetry: same agent, join vs cancel, from the home page
NaggingMeasured seeded

A dismissed popup keeps coming back

ExpectedOnce dismissed, it stays dismissed
ObservedPopup 'shopping is better on the app! get the kartiq app for app-only deals. ' reappeared on 4 later screens
  • http://127.0.0.1:5401/cart, http://127.0.0.1:5401/checkout, http://127.0.0.1:5401/checkout/review, http://127.0.0.1:5401/product/tee
Method: Repetition count of dismissed popups across the journey
False UrgencyProven seeded

ExpectedA deadline is the same moment for everyone

Declining is worded to shame the user

ExpectedNeutral decline wording
Observed"No thanks, I don't care about my stuff" on https://practicesoftwaretesting.com/checkout
  • The phrase 'I don't care about my stuff' attributes a negative sentiment to the user's values regarding their belongings, making them feel foolish or negligent for declining protection. (assessed by Ollama · qwen3.5:35b-a3b (local))
Method: Wording judgement on controls that decline an offer
Trick QuestionJudged seeded

Consent question is worded to confuse

ExpectedA plain question; optional consent off by default
Observed"Uncheck this box if you do not want to not receive offers from our partners" — selected by default
  • The label contains multiple negations that invert standard logic: 1) The base action is 'receive offers'. 2) A negative modifier creates 'not receive offers' (opting out). 3) Another negative phrase 'do not want to [not receive]' cancels the previous one, resulting in a positive meaning of 'want to
  • Assessed by Ollama · qwen3.5:35b-a3b (local)
  • The LLM and the negation-count rule disagree on what selecting it means
Method: Consent wording analysis (local LLM with reasoning) + default-state audit
Forced ActionProven seeded

To continue, the user must marketing consent checkbox labeling confusion

ExpectedCompleting the task needs only what the task needs
ObservedOn https://practicesoftwaretesting.com/checkout: "Uncheck this box if you do not want to not receive offers from our partners"
  • The site refused to continue: You must subscribe to our newsletter to check out.
Method: Careful user tries to proceed without the unrelated step; refusal recorded

Limits

  • The test shops were written alongside the engine. They differ in structure, wording, currency and mechanism, but they are not independent of it; the real-site runs are the check on that.
  • Without a site's back end, stock and deadline claims are tested from the outside (quantity probe, fresh sessions). An inventory feed in UAT makes these checks stronger.
  • Real public sites are audited read-only: no accounts, no personal data, no subscriptions, never past the payment step.
  • The hurried user is a risk indicator, not a validated model of real shoppers. Findings are evidence for legal review.
